summary.headline: Stylam Q2 FY27: new plant commissioned 22 Sep 2026; EBITDA margin ~18% (ex-other income) vs ~21% prior quarter, on ocean freight and energy costs.
summary.overview: Management said the new plant became operational on 22 September 2026, with two presses running and two more due within days, and guided to INR250-300 crore turnover from the plant this year. Management says EBITDA margin is ~18% when export incentives are kept in operating profit; the call cited ocean freight and energy costs as the main headwind, with about 3-3.5% of margin impact. Export realisation rose to INR191/kg in Q2 from INR186 in Q1 and INR161 a year earlier, while domestic volumes fell because the company stopped selling low-value liner products. Management declined to guide on near-term margins, citing the Middle East war and raw material volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (management basis, export incentives in operating profit)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~21% in Q1 FY27 per analyst; management says H1 FY27 margin is better than H1 FY26
vs INR186/kg in Q1 FY27 and INR161/kg a year ago (~19-20% YoY)

financial_highlights.value: ~16% YoY (as cited by analyst, not disputed by management)
INR77 crore in Q2 FY27 (per analyst)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR58 crore in Q1 FY27; management attributed INR11 crore of the increase to ocean freight and PNG/fuel costs
vs 5.83 million sheets in H1 FY26
FY26 full year INR3 crore; management cited forward-contract losses of INR7-8 crore in H1 FY26 that did not recur

segments.name: Exports (HPL)
segments.commentary: Export volumes grew strongly in H1 (analyst cited 30-35%), with realisation up to INR191/kg in Q2. Management said Middle East and Europe container availability caused a 2-3% shortfall in Q2 sales; the situation has improved from worse to better.

segments.name: Domestic laminates
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes dipped as the company stopped selling commodity liners (previously ~300,000 sheets per month) to focus on value-added products. Management says the domestic revamp will show drastic change in Q3 and Q4 FY27; some price increases taken, but domestic share is small.

segments.name: Solid acrylic surfaces
segments.commentary: Essentially no domestic or export sales in the last 2-3 years; management is treating the business as a fresh start, with changes expected within 1-2 quarters. No synergy with Aica Kogyo identified yet.

guidance_outlook: New plant turnover expected at INR250-300 crore in FY27.
New plant utilisation expected at 25-30% in FY27 and 60-70%+ in FY28.
Management declined to give quarterly EBITDA margin guidance, citing the war and raw material volatility; it said it will at least hold current margins.
Per-kg export realisation and tonnage disclosure to start from Q3 FY27.
Domestic revamp expected to show visible change in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: New plant (same location) operational from 22 Sep 2026; two presses running, third and fourth due within days; full operation expected within the month of November.
Management expects only a few weeks of ramp-up issues; the product is not new, so no long stabilisation period is expected.
Remaining work includes an outer wall and road improvements linked to the new plant; CWIP INR12.41 crore relates primarily to it.
Upgrades and bottleneck-removal are underway at both old plants to add capacity.
Management expects little incremental fixed cost from the new plant; cost increases are mainly direct costs and maintenance cost is expected to be near zero for 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: Export competition has shifted to local unorganised Indian players as well as organised players, which limits export price increases.
Domestic price increases were taken, but domestic share is small; management said export price push is difficult.
Management says European and other global manufacturers are losing share to Indian producers due to energy, labour and raw material costs.
Raw material prices are at a peak; management described part of the pricing as trader/supplier cartel behaviour.
Aica Kogyo partnership has been active for ~4 months (joined mid-June 2026); no concrete joint opportunities yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why does export realisation per sheet rise only ~1% YoY when freight and chemical costs rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-kg is the right metric: Q2 export realisation was INR191/kg vs INR161/kg a year ago (~19-20% up); per-sheet data (1,039 to 1,052) reflects mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 17% and other expenses rise ~40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is 18%+ because export incentives are operating income, not other income. It declined to guide on future margins, citing crude and raw material volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross/contribution margin hold with the new plant ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will hold at least current margins, expects only a few weeks of ramp-up issues, and sees margins improving as utilisation rises and raw material costs fall.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the other expense increase is due to freight and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ocean freight was INR8.15 crore and PNG cost was INR2.5 crore (INR11 crore total); the rest scales with volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall from INR9 crore in H1 FY26 to INR3 crore for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to forward-contract losses of INR7-8 crore in H1 FY26 that did not recur; surplus cash was used for the new plant and working-capital limits are now being used.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash from operations include a INR15 crore swing in other current financial liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not answer on the call and said it would reply by email.

risks_watch: Middle East and European shipping: container and vessel availability, ocean freight costs, and risk of renewed airspace/port closures that could halt Gulf shipments.
Energy (PNG, pet coke, coal) and raw material costs; management gave no margin guidance.
Domestic revamp execution: volumes fell as liners were dropped, and the Q3/Q4 recovery is still unproven.
New plant ramp: utilisation target of 25-30% this year depends on export orders that are constrained by logistics.
Unanswered items: the INR15 crore change in other current financial liabilities in operating cash flow and the revenue growth breakup (price vs mix vs volume).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the new plant, export realisations and the domestic revamp timeline, but evasive on forward margins and price increases, which management tied to the war and raw material volatility. Several answers were deferred to email.

adds.what: New plant at same location, two presses running, two more due within days; INR250-300 crore FY27 turnover expected

growth.why: Management guides INR250-300 crore new-plant turnover in FY27 at 25-30% utilisation, backed by a plant commissioned 22 Sep 2026 with presses ramping, while margin guidance was withdrawn due to war and raw-material volatility.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin ~18% in Q2 vs ~21% in Q1 on ocean freight and energy costs (3-3.5% margin impact), and management declined to guide on near-term margins, though it says it will at least hold current margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New plant at the same location became operational 22 Sep 2026 with two presses running and two more due within days, full operation expected in November; FY27 turnover guided at INR250-300 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 sheet volume 6.96 million vs 5.83 million in H1 FY26 (~19% up), new plant utilisation guided at 25-30% in FY27 and 60-70%+ in FY28, though export logistics caused a 2-3% Q2 shortfall and domestic liners were dropped (~300,000 sheets/month).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is upgrading and debottlenecking both old plants, and new plant utilisation only reaches 60-70%+ in FY28, but no new greenfield capex was announced on the call and the new plant is not yet at full utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held new-plant FY27 guidance (INR250-300 crore, 25-30% utilisation) and withdrew margin guidance citing the war and raw material volatility, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was withdrawn, other expenses rose to INR77 crore from INR58 crore (INR11 crore from freight and PNG), and the Q2 export shortfall of 2-3% was tied to container availability in Middle East and Europe.

rows.label: Export price increases limited by competition
rows.why: Export competition has shifted to local unorganised and organised Indian players, and management said export price push is difficult; export realisation rose only INR186 to INR191/kg QoQ.

rows.label: Domestic laminates revamp shows change in Q3-Q4 FY27
rows.why: Commodity liners (~300,000 sheets/month) were dropped and management says the domestic revamp will show drastic change in Q3 and Q4 FY27, though domestic share is small and the recovery is unproven.

rows.label: Solid acrylic surfaces restart
rows.why: The business had essentially no domestic or export sales in the last 2-3 years, and management expects changes within 1-2 quarters; no Aica Kogyo synergy identified yet, and no revenue number was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the new plant, export realisation and the domestic revamp timeline, but cautious on forward margins and price increases, which it tied to the war and raw material volatility; several answers, including the INR15 crore other-liabilities swing, were deferred to email while
